content:
The image shows corn stalks near the base with distinctive discoloration on the leaf sheath. Key observations:

- Dark lesions on the stalk and leaf collar/sheath area
- Color ranges from purple/dark brown to tan/bleached patches on the lower stalk and leaf sheath
- The lesions appear at the leaf collar and lower stalk area
- Affected plants are in a field setting
- The damage is concentrated at the leaf sheath/collar junction on the stalk
- There is a reddish-purple to brown-black coloration on the stalk nodes/sheath area

This pattern of dark purple-to-brown-black lesions on the leaf sheath and stalk collar, with pieces of debris potentially in the leaf collar, is characteristic of **Purple Leaf Sheath**. The symptom description matches: "Dark lesions on corn stalks and leaf collars, with color varying from purple to brown to black."

The lesions are not typical of stalk rots (no soft/mushy tissue), not rust (no pustules), not leaf blight (lesions are on sheath/collar not leaf blade), and not smut (no galls or spore masses).
